summary: Ship the daemon as one multi-arch OCI image (ghcr.io/insforge/instacloud:<version>: Node 22 bookworm-slim, GNU coreutils for cp --reflink, docker CLI copied from the docker:<v>-cli image, built ui/dist, templates/ manifests, run via tsx), a three-service compose stack (instad: network_mode host + docker.sock + the data dir bind-mounted at the IDENTICAL host path; edge: Caddy 2 in host mode with on-demand TLS gated by a loopback-only ask endpoint the daemon serves outside its API, ACME with internal-issuer fallback; garage: dxflrs/garage:v2.3.0 as container io-garage on bind-mounted dirs), a POSIX-sh install.sh that is also the upgrader (root+Linux check, refuse busy 80/443/5432, install Docker, /var/lib/instacloud with a reflink probe and an XFS reflink=1 loop image fallback mounted over it, public IP to <ip-dashes>.sslip.io, writes /etc/instacloud/{instad.env,compose.yml,Caddyfile} and the Garage toml, compose up, waits on /healthz, prints the setup URL), and a tag-triggered GitHub workflow publishing linux/amd64+arm64. Local mode (git clone, npm run dev, 127.0.0.1:8080, ~/.insta-oss, no auth, no edge) is untouched; INSTA_OSS_MODE defaults to local and the image sets server. No API route is added: the only new HTTP surface is the loopback ask listener, which is daemon-internal configuration for the edge, never reachable on api.<domain>.

Existing knobs that stay as overrides: INSTA_OSS_STATE (state.ts:17), INSTA_OSS_UI_DIST (server.ts:671), INSTA_OSS_PORT (main.ts:13). Local-mode defaults: mode local, domain localhost, data dir ~/.insta-oss, port 8080, no internal listener, no TLS. Config rule the reconciler must keep: in server mode every path the daemon hands to `docker -v`/`--mount` is under INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR, which is bind-mounted at the same absolute path inside the daemon container, so host-path and in-container path are one string.
sharedSurface.engineSeams: (1) `Engine.ownsHostname(host)` as above, called by src/internal.ts. (2) main.ts: `startInternal(engine, cfg)` after listen in server mode. (3) LocalGarage.ensure(): server mode never `docker run`s io-garage (compose owns it; container_name io-garage matches garage.ts:15). (4) Router WP constraints that packaging imposes: instad runs with network_mode host, and Docker REFUSES `docker network connect <branch-net> <host-mode container>` (daemon error: 'container sharing network namespace with another container or host cannot be connected to any other network'), so the in-network TCP lane cannot be implemented by joining branch networks with aliases (spec section 3 'TCP lane, in-network' as written). Design within host mode: the router listens on 0.0.0.0:<lane port> and identifies the calling branch by `socket.localAddress` = that branch network's gateway IP (`docker network inspect -f '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}' io-<ref>`, cached per branch); the compute adapter adds `--add-host <service>-<ref>.<domain>:<gateway>` for every lane hostname of the branch at deploy so apps resolve the in-network name to the gateway; the HTTP lane dials container IPs from `docker inspect -f '{{.NetworkSettings.Networks.io-<ref>.IPAddress}}'` (embedded DNS is not available from the host netns) and re-resolves on ECONNREFUSED after a wake (IP changes on docker start). (5) Certificate seam for the TCP lanes: Caddy's store layout is `${INSTA_OSS_TLS_CERT_DIR}/<issuer>/<host>/<host>.crt|.key` with issuer dirs `acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org-directory` and `local`; a hostname that has never been visited over HTTPS has no cert, so the router triggers issuance by opening a TLS connection to 127.0.0.1:443 with servername=<host> (Caddy on-demand issues during that handshake, bounded 15 s), then loads the files; re-read on mtime change (Caddy renews in place). (6) Scheduler WP: free-RAM reads /proc/meminfo, which shows HOST values inside the container (no lxcfs), and `docker stats` works through the socket; the daemon's own container is never an eviction candidate (only `io-<ref>-*` names).

algorithm:
A. Compose stack (/etc/instacloud/compose.yml, written verbatim by install.sh; operator customisation goes in compose.override.yml which compose auto-merges because the script runs `cd /etc/instacloud && docker compose ...`):
```
name: instacloud
services:
  instad:
    image: ${INSTA_IMAGE}:${INSTA_VERSION}
    container_name: io-instad
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host            # binds 127.0.0.1:8080 (HTTP lane/API), 127.0.0.1:8081 (ask), 0.0.0.0:5432/6379/3306/27017 (TCP lanes); reaches bridge container IPs directly
    init: true                    # reaps docker CLI children
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    env_file: instad.env
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - ${INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR}:${INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR}   # identical path: every -v the daemon emits is valid on the host
  edge:
    image: caddy:2.10.2           # verify exact patch tag exists at implementation
    container_name: io-edge
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host            # 80/443 without NAT; real client IPs; reaches 127.0.0.1:8080 and :8081
    depends_on: [instad]
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - ${INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR}/caddy/data:/data       # certificate store; router reads it via INSTA_OSS_TLS_CERT_DIR
      - ${INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR}/caddy/config:/config
  garage:
    image: dxflrs/garage:v2.3.0   # same pin as src/adapters/garage.ts:16
    container_name: io-garage     # MUST equal the GARAGE constant, garage.ts:15; the adapter finds and starts it
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - 127.0.0.1:3900:3900       # daemon's SigV4 calls, garage.ts:197-204
      - 127.0.0.1:3902:3902       # public-bucket web endpoint; router proxies <bucket>.s3.<domain> here
    volumes:
      - ${INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR}/garage/garage.toml:/etc/garage.toml:ro
      - ${INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR}/garage/meta:/var/lib/garage/meta
      - ${INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR}/garage/data:/var/lib/garage/data
```
Garage stays on the compose bridge network (not host) because the daemon `docker network connect`s it to every branch network (garage.ts:151) and apps reach it as http://io-garage:3900 (garage.ts:165); that connect is legal for a bridge container.

B. Caddyfile (/etc/instacloud/Caddyfile; concrete values, no env placeholders, because `email` with an empty placeholder fails to parse):
```
{
	admin off
	email <INSTA_ACME_EMAIL or omitted line>
	on_demand_tls {
		ask http://127.0.0.1:8081/tls/ask
	}
}
https:// {
	tls {
		on_demand
		issuer acme            # omitted when INSTA_TLS_MODE=internal
		issuer internal        # fallback: Caddy tries issuers in order; a rate-limited or unreachable ACME yields a self-signed leaf (12 h lifetime, re-tries ACME on renewal)
	}
	encode zstd gzip
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 {
		header_up X-Forwarded-Proto https
		header_up X-Forwarded-Host {host}
		flush_interval -1          # SSE/WebSocket/log tails through the HTTP lane stream unbuffered
	}
}
http:// {
	redir https://{host}{uri} permanent   # Caddy's ACME HTTP-01 solver takes precedence on :80 before this route
}
```
Per-host certificates only (sslip.io has no wildcard support). Caddy's built-in on-demand throttling applies; the ask hook is the abuse control: only hostnames the daemon owns are issued.

C. Garage config the installer writes once (${DATA}/garage/garage.toml; keys mirror garage.ts:40-56 with the install domain): metadata_dir=/var/lib/garage/meta, data_dir=/var/lib/garage/data, db_engine=sqlite, replication_factor=1, rpc_bind_addr=[::]:3901, rpc_secret=<64 hex, generated once>, [s3_api] s3_region=garage, api_bind_addr=[::]:3900, root_domain=.s3.<domain>, [s3_web] bind_addr=[::]:3902, root_domain=.web.<domain>, index=index.html. On a domain change (re-run with --domain) the script rewrites ONLY the two root_domain lines with sed and keeps rpc_secret.

D. install.sh, step by step (POSIX sh, set -eu):
0. Constants: CFG=/etc/instacloud, DATA=/var/lib/instacloud, IMG=/var/lib/instacloud.img, ENV=$CFG/instad.env, IMAGE=ghcr.io/insforge/instacloud, REPO=InsForge/insta-oss. Flags: --domain <d>, --email <e>, --version <vX.Y.Z>, --tls acme|internal, --data-img-gib <n>, --print-env|--print-compose|--print-caddyfile, -y. Env equivalents: INSTA_DOMAIN, INSTA_ACME_EMAIL, INSTA_VERSION, INSTA_TLS_MODE, INSTA_DATA_IMG_GIB, INSTA_PUBLIC_IP (test/override). Flag wins over env; env wins over an existing instad.env value; existing value wins over the default.
1. --print-* modes: compute DOMAIN/SECRET from env or placeholders, render the requested heredoc to stdout, exit 0. No root, no side effects.
2. Preconditions: `id -u` = 0 else 'run as root: curl ... | sudo sh'; `uname -s` = Linux; `uname -m` in x86_64|aarch64; require curl (apt-get/dnf install if missing), iproute2 (`ss`), xfsprogs (installed lazily in step 5 only when the loop image is needed). UPGRADE=1 when $ENV exists.
3. Ports: STACK_UP=1 when `docker compose ps -q` (in $CFG, if docker exists) prints anything. If STACK_UP=0: for p in 80 443 5432: `ss -Hltn "sport = :$p"` non-empty -> refuse: 'port $p is in use (holder: $(ss -Hltnp ...)); stop it or set it free, then re-run'. For 6379 3306 27017: warn only ('the <type> lane will not bind; managed <type> databases stay reachable in-network only').
4. Docker: if no `docker` -> `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh`; `systemctl enable --now docker` when systemctl exists; require `docker compose version` (plugin ships with get.docker.com; on failure print the distro package name docker-compose-plugin and exit).
5. Data dir and reflinks: `mkdir -p $DATA`. If $IMG exists and `! mountpoint -q $DATA` -> `mount $DATA` (fstab from a prior run). Probe: `: > $DATA/.reflink.a && cp --reflink=always $DATA/.reflink.a $DATA/.reflink.b`; rm both. Success -> REFLINK=native. Failure and $DATA non-empty and no $IMG (an older install on ext4) -> print 'reflinks unavailable; branch clones will stream pg_basebackup; to convert, stop the stack, move /var/lib/instacloud aside, re-run, move data back' and continue. Failure and $DATA empty -> build the image: apt-get/dnf install xfsprogs if `mkfs.xfs` missing; FREE=`df -BG --output=avail /var/lib | tail -1 | tr -dc 0-9`; FREE < 15 -> refuse ('need 15 GiB free under /var/lib'); SIZE=${INSTA_DATA_IMG_GIB:-$((FREE-5))} (never below 10); `truncate -s ${SIZE}G $IMG` (sparse: costs nothing until used); `mkfs.xfs -q -m reflink=1 $IMG`; append to /etc/fstab `$IMG $DATA xfs loop,nofail 0 0` unless present; `mount $DATA`; re-run the probe and abort if it still fails. (Loop mounts from fstab are part of local-fs.target, ordered before docker.service, so reboots are safe; nofail keeps a damaged image from blocking boot.) Then `mkdir -p $DATA/pg $DATA/vol $DATA/garage/meta $DATA/garage/data $DATA/caddy/data $DATA/caddy/config`.
6. Domain: DOMAIN = --domain | INSTA_DOMAIN | existing INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN in $ENV | auto. Auto: IP = INSTA_PUBLIC_IP | `curl -4 -fsS --max-time 5 https://api.ipify.org` | `curl -4 -fsS --max-time 5 https://ifconfig.me/ip` | `ip -4 route get 1.1.1.1 | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i==\"src\") print $(i+1); exit}'`; validate dotted quad; DOMAIN=`printf %s $IP | tr . -`.sslip.io. If a private-range IP was the only answer, warn that certificates will fall back to self-signed until a public name exists.
7. Secrets and files: SECRET = existing INSTA_OSS_SECRET | `head -c 32 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \\n'`. RPC secret the same way. Write $DATA/garage/garage.toml if absent (section C), else patch root_domain lines when DOMAIN changed. VERSION = --version | INSTA_VERSION | resolve `https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases/latest` tag (sed pattern from insta-cli/install.sh:64) | `latest`; strip the leading v for the image tag. TLS_MODE = --tls | INSTA_TLS_MODE | existing | acme. Write $ENV: on a fresh install the full file from the config block; on upgrade, for each key in the block, keep the existing line if present (values the operator edited survive) and append missing keys with defaults; always set INSTA_VERSION, INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN, INSTA_TLS_MODE, INSTA_ACME_EMAIL from the resolved values; `chmod 600 $ENV`. Write $CFG/compose.yml and $CFG/Caddyfile from the heredocs, always overwritten (they are the product's; overrides go in compose.override.yml).
8. Up: `cd $CFG && docker compose --env-file instad.env pull && docker compose --env-file instad.env up -d --remove-orphans`. Branch containers (`io-<ref>-*`, `--restart unless-stopped`) are not part of the project and keep running across an instad recreate.
9. Readiness: poll `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz` every 2 s up to 60 s; on timeout print `docker compose logs instad` tail and exit 1.
10. Print exactly:
```
InstaCloud is running.
  Setup:    https://console.<DOMAIN>/setup
  API:      https://api.<DOMAIN>
  CLI:      insta login --api-key <token from the setup page> --api-url https://api.<DOMAIN>
  Config /etc/instacloud   Data /var/lib/instacloud   Reflinks: native|loop image (<SIZE> GiB)|unavailable
Re-run this script to upgrade (add --version vX.Y.Z to pin).
```
The first HTTPS visit takes a few seconds while the edge issues the certificate.

E. Upgrade = re-run: steps 2 to 10 with UPGRADE=1; step 3 is skipped when the stack is up; step 5 only mounts; step 7 merges; step 8 recreates only services whose image or config changed. Rollback: re-run with the previous --version.

F. Local (laptop) flow, unchanged: `git clone && npm install && npm run build:ui && npm run dev` (README.md:57-63); INSTA_OSS_MODE unset -> local; daemon binds 127.0.0.1:8080 (main.ts:21), no edge, no auth, no internal listener, state in ~/.insta-oss (state.ts:17), Garage self-started with named volumes (garage.ts:69-77). Nothing in this WP changes those code paths; the image merely sets INSTA_OSS_MODE=server.

G. Release: `npm version <x.y.z>` commits + tags v<x.y.z> on main; push tag -> release-image.yml builds linux/amd64,linux/arm64 and pushes :<x.y.z>, :<x.y>, :latest (non-prerelease), :sha-<sha>; the tag/package.json equality guard fails the job on drift. install.sh resolves the newest GitHub release, so publishing the GitHub release (not just the tag) is what makes an upgrade visible; a draft release is invisible.

risks: network_mode host (fixed decision 2) makes `docker network connect` to branch networks impossible for the daemon container (Docker refuses for host-namespace containers), which contradicts the spec's in-network lane as written (spec section 3, 'joins every branch network ... network alias'). The router WP must route by the branch network's gateway address (socket.localAddress) and inject --add-host at deploy, and dial containers by inspected IP instead of embedded DNS. Flagged in engineSeams; the reconciler must pick this up before the router is implemented.

postgres.ts:4 hard-codes POSTGRES_PASSWORD=insta; with the router's 5432 lane on a public IP that is a remote-root database for anyone who guesses a hostname. The branching/router WP must mint a per-branch random password (like managed DBs, engine.ts:84) before the lane goes public; packaging does not open 5432 by itself but install.sh reserves it.

Running tsx in production: startup cost (~300 ms) and a TypeScript transformer in the runtime path. Acceptable now; the escape hatch is a single esbuild bundle (one devDependency) or switching tsconfig to NodeNext with .js import suffixes. Either is a later, mechanical change.

Let's Encrypt limits are per registered domain; if sslip.io is not on the Public Suffix List, every self-host install shares one quota and ACME fails under load, leaving installs on the internal issuer (browser warnings). The docs say 'production needs a real domain' (spec Known gaps) and --domain is first-class.

The loop image is sparse and sized from free space at install time; it cannot grow past the root filesystem, and XFS on a full loop file fails writes hard (Postgres then stops cleanly on SIGTERM but branches cannot be created). Docs carry the truncate + xfs_growfs recipe; the scheduler/observability WPs should surface disk free from statvfs of the data dir.

Caddy on-demand issuance happens on the first HTTPS handshake; for the TCP lanes (5432 with SNI) the router must trigger issuance itself (engineSeams item 5) or the first psql connection to a never-visited branch sees a handshake failure. Bounded by Caddy's issuance time (2 to 10 s).

`docker compose down` or a manual `docker rm io-instad` never touches branch containers, but README's cleanup line `docker ps -aq --filter name=io- | xargs docker rm -f` (README.md:157) now also kills io-instad and io-edge on a server; the README edit must scope it.
get.docker.com is a moving script; on an unsupported distro the installer stops with the vendor's error. Supported target is Ubuntu 22.04+/Debian 12+ (spec line 122); others are best-effort.

Same-path bind rule: if an operator edits INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR in instad.env without moving the data, compose (which interpolates the same variable into the bind) mounts an empty directory and the daemon starts with empty state. install.sh refuses a changed INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR on upgrade unless --data-dir is passed explicitly (documented).

The Garage toml root_domain values (.s3.<domain>, .web.<domain>) are written by the installer but consumed by the garage/router WPs; if those WPs choose a different public bucket hostname shape the installer heredoc must follow. Kept parallel to garage.ts:50-53 deliberately.
